sentence: Studies how very thin wires made of perovskite semiconductors form and grow, and how to control their size and quality.
Tests whether Scarlet Monkeyflower populations grew faster because natural selection helped them adapt during a long drought.
Builds a control system based on deep neural networks that lets a home exoskeleton be run from a distant computer despite delays.
Builds a deep learning model that works out how blood moves and what pressure it has inside blood vessels from static medical images.
Develops mathematical theory and statistical methods for deep learning, generative AI models and the study of genomics and single-cell technologies.
Looks in a laboratory tank for twisted swirls in gravity-driven slope flows to test whether their collisions trigger turbulence.
Uses seafloor seismometer data to study what controls earthquakes on an ocean transform fault where earthquakes repeat about every five years.
Studies which factors shape how well secondary mathematics teachers teach and whether they stay at a school, move or leave the profession early.
Builds a hub where electron and scanning probe microscopes guided by AI carry out experiments on their own to study materials at the nanoscale.
Studies how plant chemistry and leaf-associated microbes shape the behavior of herbivores and their predators in natural and agricultural settings.
Brings researchers together to discuss how to keep computer systems secure and private, including ways AI can help with security.
Studies how water underground links melting glaciers to mountain streams and whether it keeps streams flowing as the climate warms.
Uses abstract algebra to extend Khovanov homology into tools that describe three-dimensional and four-dimensional shapes called manifolds.
Builds tiny amplifiers from nanowires of superconductor and semiconductor materials that work in the microwave range for use in quantum technology.
Studies how ice and snow cover and winter conditions change the plankton and food webs of lakes across the whole year.
